summary:
PredSphere is an interactive Earth-observation platform that helps users discover, measure, and understand environmental change using real NASA data. We developed a 3D globe interface where users can explore variables such as surface temperature, vegetation, water and ice, and atmospheric carbon across different locations and time periods.

The platform combines visual exploration with rigorous statistical analysis. Users can inspect local time series, calculate Sen’s slope, run the Mann–Kendall trend test, view p-values, and determine whether an observed trend is statistically meaningful. SphereBot provides conversational explanations of the results, making complex climate statistics accessible to students, researchers, and the public.

PredSphere addresses the challenge by transforming complex, fragmented Earth-science data into an intuitive evidence-based experience. It is important because recognizing environmental change is not enough—we must also measure it, test its significance, and communicate it clearly so that better scientific understanding and decisions can follow.
details:
PredSphere is an interactive Earth-observation platform designed to make environmental change easier to explore, measure, and understand.

The project presents Earth as a 3D interactive globe. Users can rotate around the planet, explore different locations, change the observation year, adjust the timeline, and switch between environmental variables such as surface temperature, vegetation, water and ice, and atmospheric carbon. The globe uses visual layers, heat maps, hexagonal observation cells, satellite indicators, and animated time-based changes to reveal geographic patterns.

When a user selects a location, PredSphere opens an inspection panel containing the underlying time series, source information, yearly values, trend direction, Sen’s slope, Mann–Kendall statistics, and p-value. This allows users to move beyond simply seeing a visual pattern and investigate whether that pattern is statistically meaningful. SphereBot provides a conversational interface for asking questions about the selected chart and explains technical results in accessible language.

The main benefit is that PredSphere connects visualization, statistical analysis, and explanation in one workflow. It is intended for students, researchers, educators, policymakers, and anyone interested in understanding how Earth systems are changing. Its impact is to make NASA Earth-observation data more approachable while encouraging evidence-based interpretation instead of relying only on visual impressions.

The frontend was developed using React, TypeScript, Vite, Three.js, Globe.gl, and custom CSS-based visualization components. The backend was built with C# and .NET, with API services for observation data, trend analysis, and SphereBot integration. We used real Earth-science data sources and NASA-related observation products, including temperature, vegetation, water and ice, and atmospheric measurements. The application is designed to run in a modern web browser using GPU-accelerated rendering; no specialized hardware is required.

The creative aspect of PredSphere is its combination of a cinematic 3D Earth interface, animated observation layers, statistical trend detection, and conversational scientific interpretation. Rather than presenting climate information as a static dashboard, it creates an exploratory experience where every visual signal can lead to a measurable result.

During development, we considered scientific accuracy, data provenance, unit consistency, statistical reliability, performance with large geospatial datasets, accessibility for non-technical users, responsive layouts, clear English language, and the need to distinguish correlation or trend from causation. Our central design principle was simple: users should be able to move from seeing a change, to measuring it, to testing it, and finally to understanding it.
